steps.description: HR and the employee's manager jointly document the performance goals and success criteria at the start of the 90-day PIP period.

evidence.quote: HR and the employee's manager jointly document the performance goals and success criteria at the start of the PIP period

steps.description: At day 60, HR and the manager conduct a mid-point check-in to assess progress and provide feedback.

evidence.quote: At day 60 of the PIP, HR and the manager conduct a mid-point check-in to assess progress and provide feedback to the employee.

steps.description: At day 90, HR and the manager assess the employee's performance and determine the outcome.

evidence.quote: At day 90, HR and the manager assess the employee's performance.

steps.description: The PIP is closed and a summary note is added to the employee's HR file.

evidence.quote: If goals are met, the PIP is closed and a summary note is added to the employee's HR file.

steps.description: The PIP is extended by 30 days. This extension may only occur once.

evidence.quote: If goals are partially met, the PIP may be extended by 30 days; this extension may only occur once.

steps.description: HR initiates a termination recommendation when performance goals are not met.

evidence.quote: If goals are not met, HR initiates a termination recommendation.

steps.description: Legal reviews the termination recommendation before it is submitted to senior leadership.

evidence.quote: Legal must review any termination recommendation before it is submitted to senior leadership for action.

steps.description: The termination recommendation is submitted to senior leadership for action after Legal review.

evidence.quote: before it is submitted to senior leadership for action

refusalTraps.reason: hypothetical proposal to skip mandatory mid-point check-in
